# Wyrd

> Wyrd is the only real-time verification system built for your applications. Before an application acts, it asks Wyrd whether the action meets the requirements you declare; Wyrd returns a verdict for each, with a reason and the exact versions it judged, and the application decides. Open source: Declare. Observe. Verify.

## Start here

Set up a local server, run one verification, then choose what to build, in this order. A connected Wyrd MCP server teaches the same route through `wyrd.guide {"topic":"start"}`.

- [Set up Wyrd](/wyrd/get-started/setup/): install Wyrd, start a local server you keep running, and check it with a verification that needs no model.
- [Run your first verification](/wyrd/get-started/quickstart/): verify each proposed finance report release against three requirements, one judged by a model reading a policy PDF, and release only a passed one, from Python, Rust, or TypeScript.
- [What can I build?](/wyrd/get-started/what-can-i-build/): example workflows built from the primitives, not a complete list: policy documents, agent evaluation, long-running workflows, runtime checks, observability, or drift.

## Home

- [Wyrd docs](/wyrd/): the docs home, with a link to each published section.

## Get started

- [What Wyrd does](/wyrd/get-started/introduction/): The only real-time verification system built for your applications. Your application asks Wyrd whether an action meets your requirements, and acts on the verdict.
- [Set up Wyrd](/wyrd/get-started/setup/): Install the Wyrd 0.4.2 CLI and SDK for Python, Rust, or TypeScript, start a local server with your coding agent or by hand, and check it with a verification that needs no model.
- [Run your first verification](/wyrd/get-started/quickstart/): Verify a finance report against three requirements, including a model that reads a sharing policy PDF, in one call, and release it only when the verdict passes. Python, Rust, or TypeScript.
- [What can I build?](/wyrd/get-started/what-can-i-build/): Example verification workflows built from Wyrd's primitives - policy documents, agent evaluation, long-running workflows, runtime checks, observability, and drift.
- [Use with your coding agent](/wyrd/get-started/use-with-your-coding-agent/): Give your coding agent the Wyrd docs through llms.txt and Wyrd's tools through MCP with wyrd mcp install.

## Build and verify

- [Write verifiable requirements](/wyrd/build-and-verify/declare/write-verifiable-requirements/): Turn a vague goal such as "the agent should be reliable" into scoped requirements with named evidence, a suitable check, tested model judges, and versioned changes.
- [Services](/wyrd/build-and-verify/declare/define-a-service/): Declare a Service from YAML files, with its components and a table for the rows it records, then read back the exact versions the server stored.
- [Bindings](/wyrd/build-and-verify/declare/bind-a-verifier/): Attach a Verifier to a Service or one of its components with verified_by, and choose whether your code or a schedule runs it.
- [Author in code](/wyrd/build-and-verify/declare/author-in-code/): Build a Service, its Agent and Prompt, and a Verifier in Python, Rust, or TypeScript, declare them without versions, verify two answers, and read back the rows each Run wrote.
- [Runs and observations](/wyrd/build-and-verify/observe/record-a-run-and-observations/): Wrap each request in a Run, call your model through the gateway, record what happened, verify it, and read the whole Run back.
- [Establish sufficient evidence](/wyrd/build-and-verify/observe/establish-sufficient-evidence/): Give each requirement evidence from its source, with citations, exact versions, and complete inputs, and tell missing evidence apart from a failure.
- [Write a Verifier](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/author-a-verifier/): Write a Verifier, bind it to your Service, call it from your code, and read its verdict, then add a Python check and a model judge.
- [Recipes](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/verifier-recipes/): Copyable Verifiers for common checks, each with its YAML and the Python that calls it - assertions, traces, Python checks, model judges, multi-step, uploaded files, grouped sessions, and drift.
- [Verify during a request](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/verify-a-request-in-real-time/): Call the Quickstart's release check from a web API, send a report only after its verdict passes, and hold every other outcome with the reason.
- [Verify an agent's workflow](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/verify-an-agent-workflow/): Catch an agent that skipped a required step even though its answer looks right, by checking the trace of the work behind the answer.
- [Investigate a failed verification](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/run-a-verification-and-inspect-its-evidence/): Find a stored failed result, read which requirement failed, the evidence it judged, and the exact Verifier and subject versions, without rerunning any check.
- [Check on a schedule](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/monitor-drift/): Have the Wyrd server judge a Service's recorded samples every minute, then read which windows passed, failed, or had no evidence.
- [Act on verdicts in production](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/act-on-verdicts-in-production/): Handle passed, failed, inconclusive, errors, and timeouts explicitly, decide what model providers may see, and measure latency and cost for the Verifier you deploy.

## Connect

- [LLM gateway](/wyrd/connect/set-up-the-llm-gateway/): Store a provider key on your Wyrd server, create a deployment for it, and call the model through Wyrd with your Wyrd credential.
- [ASGI apps](/wyrd/connect/integrate-asgi/): Add WyrdMiddleware to a FastAPI, Starlette, Django, or Litestar app to start Wyrd with the app, verify inside one Run per request, and drain queued evidence at shutdown.

## Operate

- [Deploy for a team](/wyrd/operate/deploy-wyrd-for-a-team/): Prepare PostgreSQL with one login, migrate it, start the server, and create the first tenant.
- [Deploy a Service from CI](/wyrd/operate/deploy-a-service-from-ci/): Give CI and each Service its own key, declare and pull the Service in CI, and start the application from the bundle.
- [Add people](/wyrd/operate/add-people/): Connect your identity provider, such as Okta or Keycloak, so people sign in to Wyrd, then grant them roles.
- [Verification runtime](/wyrd/operate/configure-verification-runtime/): Choose which processes run Verifiers, size the worker pool, and diagnose startup refusals.
- [Permissions](/wyrd/operate/grant-and-inspect-permissions/): See which roles a principal holds, grant or revoke a role, cut a principal off, and confirm the result in the audit log.
- [Troubleshooting](/wyrd/operate/troubleshoot-a-deployment/): Find the cause of a Wyrd server that refuses to migrate or start, from the message it prints.

## Understand

- [Foundations of verification](/wyrd/understand/foundations-of-verification/): What AI verification establishes, how it differs from evaluation, testing, and formal proof, and how to check outputs that have no single right answer.
- [Real-time verification](/wyrd/understand/real-time-verification/): Real-time verification for AI applications: checking an action before it happens, deadlines, evidence and check time, uncertain results, and when to check later.
- [How verification works in Wyrd](/wyrd/understand/how-verification-works/): How Wyrd verifies an action against declared requirements: Verifiers, bindings, evidence, verify, submit, and schedules, where the time goes, and what is kept.
- [Runs and evidence](/wyrd/understand/runs-observations-and-evidence/): How Wyrd records what a declared service actually does, and ties each observation to the version that ran.
- [Cards and versions](/wyrd/understand/cards-versions-and-relationships/): A Service declaration is a set of versioned Cards, each one a declared component of an AI system.
- [Bifrost](/wyrd/understand/bifrost/): Wyrd's analytical warehouse, the two ways to write to it, and when a written row becomes queryable.
- [Identity and access](/wyrd/understand/identity-and-authorization/): Every call to Wyrd is made as an account whose roles decide what it may do; a running Service also names its exact release, from its bundle.
- [Architecture](/wyrd/understand/architecture/): What a team deployment of Wyrd runs, what it connects to, and why each part is separate.
- [Technical questions](/wyrd/understand/technical-questions/): Direct answers on real-time verification: who enforces a verdict, missing evidence, timeouts, model providers, sensitive data, versions, and self-hosting.

## Reference

- [Verifier Card](/wyrd/reference/verifier-card/): Fields, input slots, steps, checks, operators, references, citations, and refusals of a Verifier spec.
- [Extraction output](/wyrd/reference/extraction-output/): The JSON an extract step returns for each media format.
- [Agent tools](/wyrd/reference/agent-tools-and-authorization/): Built-in tools a Verifier's Agent can call and the permissions each call needs.
- [Runtime limits](/wyrd/reference/verification-runtime-limits/): Environment settings that bound Verifier files, extraction, workspaces, and Python code, with defaults and startup rules.
- [MCP tools](/wyrd/reference/mcp-tools/): Wyrd MCP tool names, permissions, shapes, and query limits.
- [Error codes](/wyrd/api/errors/): Every stable Wyrd error code with its HTTP status, title, and fix.
- [HTTP API](/wyrd/api/openapi/): Where a Wyrd server serves its OpenAPI document and how to use it.

## Machine-readable reference

- [llms-full.txt](/wyrd/llms-full.txt): every page below in full, with its embedded YAML and code.
